status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027 (Art. 54, second paragraph). The original OJ L 165 print said 14 Jan 2027; corrigendum OJ L 169, 4.7.2023 corrected it to 20 Jan 2027. Commission and EU-OSHA pages agree. Authentic Art. 54 wording not read by hand.
clause_or_section_seen: Art. 54, second paragraph (seen in EUR-Lex consolidated text of 27.7.2026, by extraction); corrigendum OJ L 169 item 10
requirement_paraphrase: Regulation applies from 20 January 2027 (Art. 54). Notified body provisions (Arts 26 to 42, per extraction) apply from 20 January 2024. Some provisions apply from 19 July 2023, 20 July 2024 and 20 October 2026. "Directive governs until 19 January 2027" is an inference not seen in the Regulation text.
applies_to: Manufacturers placing machinery on EU market

instrument: Machinery Reg (EU) 2023/1230 as amended by Reg 2026/1744
status_note: Per EUR-Lex consolidated text of 27 July 2026 (no legal effect); Reg (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 Jul 2026, in force 27 Jul 2026. Delegation period: five years from 27 Jul 2026 (Art. 47(2)).
clause_or_section_seen: Art. 8 (new third and fourth paragraphs), Art. 20(10), Art. 47(2) (consolidated text, markers M2)
requirement_paraphrase: Commission to adopt delegated acts amending Machinery Reg Annex III with health and safety requirements for AI systems that are high-risk under AI Act Art. 6(1) and are safety components of, or themselves, machinery, reflecting AI Act Ch. III Sec. 2 and Arts 17, 19, 72, 73; the delegated acts are to apply by 2 Aug 2028. Until harmonised standards or common specifications exist under the Machinery Reg, systems complying with standards/specifications under AI Act Arts 40/41 are presumed to meet Annex III machinery requirements.
applies_to: Machinery with AI safety components, incl. robots

instrument: Regulation (EU) No 376/2014 Reporting of occurrences in civil aviation
edition_or_version: Consolidated 2018-09-11 (EUR-Lex); UK retained version also read
requirement_paraphrase: Mandatory reporting of occurrences posing significant risk by listed persons (pilot in command, designers/maintainers, ATS staff etc.) within 72 hours; organisations must have mandatory and voluntary reporting systems.
applies_to: Persons and organisations in EU civil aviation

status_note: Entered into force 19 Jul 2023 (EUR-Lex ELI metadata; Art. 54 first paragraph, "twentieth day following" publication). Applies from 20 Jan 2027 (Art. 54), corrected from 14 Jan 2027 by corrigendum OJ L 169, 4.7.2023. Amended by Reg (EU) 2026/1744 (in force 27 Jul 2026).
requirement_paraphrase: Regulation on machinery that repeals Directive 2006/42/EC and Directive 73/361/EEC; adopted 14 Jun 2023, published 29 Jun 2023 (OJ L 165), in force 19 Jul 2023, applies from 20 Jan 2027 (the original print said 14 Jan 2027; corrected by corrigendum OJ L 169, 4.7.2023, p. 35).
applies_to: Machinery and related products placed on EU market

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023. Before that date Directive 2006/42/EC still applies to products placed on the market.
requirement_paraphrase: Manufacturer must ensure machinery is designed and built to meet the Annex III essential health and safety requirements before placing on market or putting into service.
applies_to: Manufacturers of machinery and related products

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023.
requirement_paraphrase: Before placing on the market or putting into service, manufacturer prepares Annex IV Part A technical documentation, completes Art. 25 conformity assessment (or has it done), then draws up Art. 21 EU declaration and affixes CE marking.

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023.
requirement_paraphrase: Technical documentation and EU declaration to be kept for at least 10 years after the machinery or related product is placed on the market or put into service; source code or programming logic included in the technical documentation to be supplied on reasoned request where needed to check compliance with Annex III.

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023.
requirement_paraphrase: Substantial modification (Art. 3(16)) is a physical or digital change made after placing on the market, not foreseen or planned by the manufacturer, that creates a new hazard or increases an existing risk and requires added guards/protective devices that change the safety control system, or additional measures for stability/mechanical strength. Under Art. 18(1)-(2) the person making it is treated as manufacturer, must declare conformity on its own responsibility and apply the Art. 25(2), (3) or (4) procedure. Art. 18(3): a non-professional user who substantially modifies own machinery for personal use is not treated as a manufacturer." Art. 18(1) also brings the Art. 10 manufacturer duties.
applies_to: Persons modifying machinery (incl. software-driven change); non-professional personal-use modifiers excluded (18(3))

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023.
requirement_paraphrase: Products conforming to harmonised standards whose references are published in the Official Journal are presumed to meet the Annex III requirements those standards cover.

Commission may adopt common specifications by implementing act only if standardisation requests failed or no harmonised-standard reference is expected in reasonable time; conformity to them gives presumption for covered requirements.

Machinery certified under an EU cybersecurity certification scheme (Reg. (EU) 2019/881) is presumed compliant with Annex III sections 1.1.9 and 1.2.1 (protection against corruption; safety and reliability of control systems) insofar as the certificate covers them.

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023.
requirement_paraphrase: EU declaration of conformity states the applicable Annex III requirements are fulfilled; follows Annex V Part A model; kept up to date and translated; combined declaration where several Union acts apply; signing means manufacturer takes responsibility.

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023.
requirement_paraphrase: For machinery in Annex I Part A categories, manufacturer must use module B (EU type-examination) plus C, or module H (full quality assurance), or module G (unit verification).
applies_to: Annex I Part A categories (trigger: product falls in Part A)

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023.
requirement_paraphrase: For Annex I Part B categories: module A (internal production control) allowed only if applicable harmonised standards or common specifications covering all relevant requirements are applied; otherwise module B+C, H or G is required.

status_note: Applies from 20 Jan 2027; in force since 19 Jul 2023.
requirement_paraphrase: Machinery not in Annex I uses module A (internal production control).

A category is included in Annex I Part A if, following the Art. 6(4) assessment, one of four conditions (a) to (d) is met; other categories with serious risk go to Part B. The conditions themselves were not read in detail.
